ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 3 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — David Hume

code.originalText: Review four weeks after laparoscopic sigmoid colectomy, before adjuvant chemotherapy

text.paragraph: Review four weeks after sigmoid colectomy. [S]

Mr. Hume returns four weeks after laparoscopic sigmoid colectomy with primary anastomosis. The liver MRI before surgery showed that the 9 mm lesion is a hemangioma, with no metastases. He went home on the third day. His stools are now formed, once or twice a day, with no blood, and his wounds have healed. He walks 20 minutes a day and is less tired since the two iron infusions. The pathology shows a pT3 N1a adenocarcinoma, with 1 of 22 lymph nodes involved, clear margins, and no lymphovascular or perineural invasion: stage IIIB. Dr. Mehta has advised three months of adjuvant CAPOX, starting next week, and sent a DPYD genotype test before the first capecitabine dose. He has been offered genetic counseling. [S]

list.item:
Resected stage IIIB sigmoid adenocarcinoma, before adjuvant therapy (C18.7). Curative resection with clear margins. CEA has fallen from 6.4 to 2.2 ng/mL, which supports complete resection. Low-risk stage III (T3 N1), for which three months of CAPOX is the evidence-based choice. Kidney and liver function allow full doses (eGFR 88). [S]
CAPOX from next week through the oncology team, if the DPYD genotype shows no decreased-function variant.
Call the oncology 24-hour line for a temperature of 38.0 °C or higher; avoid acetaminophen before checking a temperature.
Primary care follows neuropathy, blood counts, mood, and survivorship planning.

Iron deficiency anemia, iron replete (D50.0). Six weeks after intravenous iron, ferritin is 186 ng/mL and transferrin saturation 24 percent. Hemoglobin has risen from 10.3 to 12.4 g/dL and should continue to recover now the bleeding source is removed. [S]
No further iron.
Blood counts with chemotherapy and at the end of treatment.

Hemangioma of the liver (D18.03). Benign incidental finding on MRI; not a metastasis. [S]
No dedicated follow-up; it will be seen on surveillance CT.
